$comment: The one place the product's identity lives. Every other file reads these values (Node side: shared/config.mjs; extension side: the generated extension/lib/config.js). Change a value here, then run `npm run sync-config` so the extension copy, the manifest and package.json follow. `npm run rename -- <slug> "<Display Name>"` sets all of them at once. Limits: productName up to 45 characters and tagline up to 132 (Chrome's manifest limits); socketName and stateDirName up to 20 characters (they sit inside a Unix socket path capped at about 104 bytes on macOS); none of the slugs may be a Windows reserved device name such as con or nul.
tagline: Drive your real, logged-in browsers from any AI agent
$comment.nativeHostId: The Chromium native messaging host name. Lowercase letters, digits, dots and underscores only. It is written into the host manifest at install time and called by the extension's connectNative(); the two must match, which is why both read it from here.
$comment.socketName: The broker's local endpoint. On Windows this is the named pipe \\.\pipe\<socketName>; on macOS and Linux it is the file <stateDir>/<socketName>.sock. Never a TCP port: nothing in this system listens on the network.
$comment.stateDirName: Folder name for machine state (runtime token, route registry, audit log, screenshots, launcher). Windows: %LOCALAPPDATA%\<stateDirName>. macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/<stateDirName>. Linux: $XDG_STATE_HOME/<stateDirName> or ~/.local/state/<stateDirName>. Override the whole path with the BRIDGE_HOME environment variable. Also the package.json name and the systemd unit prefix on Linux.
$comment.serviceName: The always-on broker's supervisor entry on Windows: the Task Scheduler task name (no \ / : * ? " < > | characters). On macOS the launchd label is <nativeHostId>.broker and on Linux the systemd user unit is <stateDirName>-broker; neither uses this value.
$comment.mcpServerName: The key written into your agent's MCP config (~/.claude.json, ~/.cursor/mcp.json, ~/.codex/config.toml). Tool names are fixed (browser_*, bridge_*) and do not change with this.
